claims.claim: DriveThruRPG's July 2023 policy bans commercial content primarily written by AI language generators while permitting partly AI-written titles, and the platform conceded enforcement difficulty.
claims.source: Timothy Linward, Wargamer, quoting the OneBookShelf policy
claims.quote: commercial content primarily written by AI language generators

claims.claim: Kobold Press's No-AI Pledge, quoted by Mike Shea, states that the publisher does not use AI to generate text for its game design.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur / Kobold Press No-AI Pledge, quoted by Mike Shea, Sly Flourish
claims.quote: we don’t use AI to generate text for our game design
claims.page: section 'The Current State of Generative AI in TTRPGs'

claims.claim: Shea reports that among 3,700 players and GMs he surveyed, about 3 in 10 use generative AI when preparing for or playing RPGs.
claims.quote: about 3 in 10 use generative AI when preparing for or playing RPGs
claims.page: section 'The Current State of Generative AI in TTRPGs'

claims.claim: Board-game designer Elizabeth Hargrave says the AI-generated placeholder names she sees designers use are often clunky but adequate for a prototype.
claims.source: Elizabeth Hargrave to BoardGameWire, quoted by Mike Didymus-True, Rascal News
claims.quote: often clunky options but they do the job

claims.claim: A study of Reddit community AI rules finds quality and authenticity to be the concerns most frequently given as justification.
claims.source: 'AI Rules? Characterizing Reddit Community Policies Towards AI-Generated Content', arXiv
claims.quote: quality and authenticity as the most frequently mentioned concerns

claims.claim: He characterises that product's read-aloud text as second person and purple.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, tenfootpole.org review of 'Three Witches'
claims.page: review body, on the dungeon rooms

claims.claim: A commenter points out that the product's own DriveThruRPG description carries the marketplace's 'Contains AI-Generated Content' label.
A commenter says the previewed product's 'Adventure Summary' is not a summary of the adventure and its 'Players Background' provides no background.
claims.source: commenter 'Beoric', tenfootpole.org comment thread on 'Bryce rebuts – Greg Gawron'
claims.quote: which is not, in fact, a summary of the adventure

claims.claim: The same commenter says those two sections are reminiscent of ChatGPT's voice, allowing either that a model wrote them or that a human steeped in LLM writing mimicked its style.
claims.source: commenter 'Beoric', tenfootpole.org comment thread on 'Bryce rebuts – Greg Gawron'

claims.claim: That commenter's stated reason is that a model struggles to hold enough separate things in mind at once to have written a chain of clues linking a broken sword in one room to a jammed secret door in another.
claims.source: commenter 'Quentin', tenfootpole.org comment thread on 'The Snake Temple Ruins'
claims.quote: an LLM struggles to remember enough different things at once

claims.claim: He adds that such a chain involves relationships a machine cannot understand or extrapolate from.
claims.source: commenter 'Quentin', tenfootpole.org comment thread on 'The Snake Temple Ruins'
claims.quote: involving relationships it can’t understand or extrapolate from

claims.claim: The ENNIE Awards' revised policy, quoted by Rascal News, states that from the 2025-2026 submission cycle it will no longer accept any products containing generative AI or created with the assistance of large language models.
claims.source: ENNIE Awards, 'Revised Policy on Generative AI Usage', quoted by Chase Carter, Rascal News
claims.quote: no longer accept any products containing generative AI

claims.claim: The WikiProject AI Cleanup field guide states that LLM writing inflates the importance of a subject by adding statements about how arbitrary aspects of it contribute to a broader topic.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing'
claims.quote: the importance of the subject matter by adding statements about how
claims.page: section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends'

claims.claim: It cites a June 2023 revision of the article on Douéra in which a census population figure is followed by the clause that it creates a lively community within its borders.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing', quoting the Douéra article
claims.quote: creating a lively community within its borders.

claims.claim: The guide states that AI chatbots attribute opinions or claims to a vague authority and exaggerate how many sources hold them.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing'
claims.quote: AI chatbots tend to attribute opinions or claims to some vague authority
claims.page: section 'Vague attributions and overgeneralization of opinions'
